title: Fox Analyst Warns Lane Kiffin May Struggle to Gain LSU Players' Trust - NewsBreak
text:
By Manhaz Muntaha ,
32 minutes ago Ole Miss is finally heading into the playoffs for the first time in program history. But right when they needed Lane Kiffin the most, he chose to depart. Kiffin is now beginning a new chapter with LSU, yet his decision has sparked heavy criticism.
Fox Analyst Warns Lane Kiffin May Struggle To Gain LSU Players’ Trust (Image Via Instagram/@thereallanekiffin) Fox analyst Joel Klatt spoke on his show about the fallout of Kiffin’s LSU move where he questioned whether the timing made the decision truly worthwhile.
“He has the right to move,” Klatt said. “That movement and that decision has consequences. I think he’s gonna struggle with credibility at LSU in front of players. How do you get players to buy in if you’re gonna leave a team in the lurch like he’s doing to Ole Miss?
“I do not believe he has to go to LSU to win a national championship. That is a fallacy because of the reality of what’s going on in college football currently, which is that you can build a powerhouse pretty much anywhere with the right resources.”
Klatt continued by explaining that LSU could add other high-profile coaches such as Curt Cignetti, Ryan Day, Kirby Smart, Dan Lanning, and Steve Sarkisian. But once those candidates either withdrew or weren’t available, Kiffin became the top remaining target.
“And all these guys took their hand down, which made Lane the big fish in the small pond. As the pool decreased, you know, his name became bigger and bigger and bigger. He’s still a coach that has not won a conference championship in the power conferences, and he has not been to a playoff, you know, as a head coach. So, and now he’s got five of the messiest exits in the history of football.”
As Kiffin is gone, Ole Miss quickly responded by promoting defensive coordinator Pete Golding as the full-time head coach.
Bill Cowher Calls Lane Kiffin’s Move “A Disgrace” CBS Sports analyst Bill Cowher also weighed in when he appeared on The Dan Patrick Show, and he didn’t hold back while questioning Kiffin’s values as a leader. Cowher compared Kiffin’s behavior to someone constantly jumping ship whenever a better job appears, instead of staying committed to building something meaningful.
“I think what happened there is a disgrace to the coaching profession because I will just say this,” Cowher said . “ The coaching profession is about developing young men. It’s not about chasing the greener grass to somewhere else.
“It’d be an ambulance chaser and go, oh, I can fix you. And then when you fix that, let me go here and fix that. It’s about developing young men. It’s about trying to create tradition, pageantry for the institution that you work for.”
The tension escalated after Ole Miss moved up from No. 7 to No. 6 in the latest CFP rankings released on Dec. 2. Several players openly expressed disappointment, even claiming Kiffin lied during his farewell speech to the team.
While emotions remain high in Oxford, a highly anticipated showdown awaits on the calendar. Kiffin and LSU are set to return to Ole Miss in 2026 in what many expect to be one of the most intense games of that season.
